content.title: From a pitcher who won Cy Youngs four years apart to the UFC’s reigning heavyweight champ: athletes celebrating birthdays today
content.text: SportsToday’s famous athlete birthdays for April 11 include a World Series MVP, UFC’s heavyweight champion, and a Chiefs 2-time Super Bowl champAmerican League All-Star pitcher Bret Saberhagen of the Kansas City Royals fires a pitch in the first inning of the 58th All-Star Game, July 14, 1987, at Oakland Coliseum. (AP Photo/Paul Sakuma)APFamous athletes born today April 11 include former Kansas City Royals ace pitcher Bret Saberhagen, UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall, Kansas City Chiefs’ running back Clyde Edwards-Helaire, and more. Read more below for photos of famous athletes celebrating their birthdays today and learn an interesting fact about each of them.Bret Saberhagen, 62Born: April 11, 1964Former MLB pitcher Bret Saberhagen boasts a resume filled with awards and achievements. In 1985, Saberhagen won his first of two Cy Young awards, helped lead the Kansas City Royals to winning the World Series and was named the World Series MVP. He won his second Cy Young award in 1989 when he led MLB in ERA (2.16), innings pitched (262.1), wins (23), complete games (12) and WAR (9.7). Saberhagen also earned three All-Star selections and one Gold Glove award. He also pitched for the New York Mets, Colorado Rockies and Boston Red Sox. Saberhagen finished his MLB career with a 167-117 record and 3.34 ERA in 399 games.New York Mets pitcher Bret Saberhagen blows a bubble of chewing gum in the fifth inning against the Montreal Expos in New York, April 13, 1992. He gave up seven earned runs in 4 2/3 innings in the 8-2 loss to the Expos. Saberhagen, a two-time Cy Young Award winner for the Kansas City Royal, has lost both his starts in his first year with the Mets. (AP Photo/Mark Lennihan)ASSOCIATED PRESSTom Aspinall, 33Born: April 11, 1993A mixed martial artist from England, 6-foot-5, 255-pound Tom Aspinall is the current UFC heavyweight champion as of April 2026. Aspinall (15-3 record) was promoted to UFC’s new undisputed heavyweight champion in June 2025 following the retirement of reigning heavyweight champ Jon Jones. He was previously the interim heavyweight champion, a distinction he earned in November 2023, after Jones was previously unable to defend his title due to injury.England's Tom Aspinall, left, kicks Russia's Sergei Pavlovich during the first round of a heavyweight title bout at the UFC 295 mixed martial arts event Saturday, Nov. 11, 2023, in New York. Aspinall stopped Pavlovich in the first round. (AP Photo/Frank Franklin II)APMark Teixeira, 46Born: April 11, 1980Former New York Yankees first baseman Mark Teixeira helped lead the Yankees to winning the World Series in 2009, his first season with the team after signing an eight-year, $180 million contract with New York in free agency. “Tex” hit 409 home runs during his 14-year MLB career from 2003-16, which included stops with the Texas Rangers, Atlanta Braves and Los Angeles Angels. He also won five Gold Glove awards, three Silver Slugger awards and earned three All-Star selections.New York Yankees' Mark Teixeira watches his ball as he flies out with one out and two men on base in the ninth inning of a baseball game against the Seattle Mariners, Monday, Aug. 22, 2016, in Seattle. The Mariners beat the Yankees 7-5. (AP Photo/Ted S. Warren)APClyde Edwards-Helaire, 27Born: April 11, 1999Kansas City Chiefs running back Clyde Edwards-Helaire has won two Super Bowls in his first six NFL seasons. The former LSU star was selected by the Chiefs in the first round of the 2020 NFL Draft. Edwards-Helaire also played one season for the New Orleans Saints in 2024 before re-joining the Chiefs in 2025.Kansas City Chiefs running back Clyde Edwards-Helaire (25) breaks through the tackle of Buffalo Bills cornerback Dane Jackson (30) during an NFL divisional round playoff football game, Sunday, Jan. 21, 2024 in Orchard Park, NY. (AP Photo/Matt Durisko)APJason Varitek, 54Born: April 11, 1972Former Boston Red Sox catcher Jason Varitek won two World Series during his 15-year MLB career from 1997-2011. He helped lead the Red Sox to winning the World Series in 2004 and 2007, and earned three All-Star selections during his career. Varitek finished his MLB career with a .256 batting average, 193 home runs, 757 RBI and .776 OPS in 1,546 games.Boston Red Sox catcher Jason Varitek celebrates with teammates after Boston's 4-2 win over the Cleveland Indians in a baseball game Tuesday, May 24, 2011, in Cleveland. Varitek hit a two-run home run in the seventh inning. (AP Photo/Mark Duncan)ASSOCIATED PRESSTrot Nixon, 52Born: April 11, 1974Former Boston Red Sox outfielder Trot Nixon played 12 seasons in MLB from 1996-2008. He played his first 10 seasons for Boston, winning the 2004 World Series, one season for the Cleveland Indians in 2007 and his final season with the New York Mets in 2008. Nixon finished his career hitting .274 with 137 home runs and an .828 OPS in 1,092 games.Boston Red Sox right fielder Trot Nixon, who is rehabbing with the Pawtucket Red Sox, chases down a fly ball by Ottawa Lynx's Howie Clark in the first inning of a minor league baseball game at McCoy Stadium in Pawtucket, R.I., Thursday Aug. 31, 2006. Nixon, who hasn't played with the Red Sox for about a month, has been on the disabled list.
